alert().message: The text the alert sends, built on the bar where it fires, so every value in it is that bar's value. Join numbers in with `text()`, so the message cannot come out absent.
alert().id: The alert's permanent name, such as `"cross-up"`, which a host keys the alert by. Write it as a short literal and keep it when you edit the script; left out, the compiler derives one and warns with `OS8008`.
alert().title: A heading for people, which you may change freely. It is fixed before the first bar, so write it at the call as a literal.
alert().frequency: How often the alert may fire: `"oncePerBar"`, `"once"` for the first time only, or `"everyUpdate"` on every run of the forming bar, which needs `onUnconfirmed = true`. The /trading chart fires every alert at most once per bar, whatever it says.

signal().text: The marker's text, read on each bar. A text of `none` puts no marker on that bar, so no `if` is needed.
signal().color: The marker's colour, which its text is drawn in on the /trading chart. It is fixed before the first bar, so write it as a literal or an `input()`.
signal().at: Where the marker sits: `"above"` the bar, `"below"` it, or `"price"` on the bar itself. It is fixed before the first bar, like `color`.
signal().shape: The marker's form, such as a `"label"` carrying the text or an `"arrowUp"`. It is fixed before the first bar, like `color`.

print().value: The value to write to the log, of any type. To combine words and numbers, build one string with `+` and `text()`.
